steps.intro: Watch our robot jump. Can you hear a jump sound? Not yet!

steps.title: Every game sound is a recipe
steps.text: Pick a robot, a start note, a slide, and how long. Mix them up and you get a game sound!

steps.prompt: What should a jump sound do: slide up, or slide down?
steps.reveal: Lots of game jumps slide up, as if you're going up. But a jump that slides down can be funny too. You'll choose!

steps.intro: {copilot}'s turn! Press the big buttons: wobble, echo, slide and sparkle.
One of you makes a secret sound. The others close their eyes, listen, and guess!

steps.title: The Channel Problem
steps.scenario: The sound chip has four channels, and the music is using all four. Then you grab a star, and the star sound needs a channel too! What should happen?

options.label: The tune goes quiet for a moment
No star sound. Keep the music.
The music only uses three channels

steps.reveal: On the NES, sound effects often took over a music channel for a moment, so part of the music went quiet. Some composers kept a channel free instead. Both work: it's a trade-off.
steps.followUp: Which matters more in a game: the music or the sound effects? Why?

steps.intro: Make our robot's jump sound! Pick a robot, then make it slide.
Jump! Listen to your jump, your star and your bonk.
